# Coronium Reseller Kit

Open-source starter kit for building a mobile-proxy reseller dashboard on top of the Coronium API (<https://dashboard.coronium.io>).

## What this is for

You (the LLM agent) are scaffolding a proxy reseller business for someone. They sell Coronium's mobile 4G/5G proxies to their end-customers with markup. This repo gives you the pattern, examples, and exact API surface to do it in one shot.

## Where to start reading

1. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/AGENTS.md> - your instructions
2. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/PROMPT.md> - the prompts the human will paste
3. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/billing-and-reconciliation.md> - charged amount, coupon before/after, carrier, webhook receipt
4. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/p0f-and-openvpn.md> - p0f stock per region, `require: ["p0f"]`, OpenVPN download answers
5. <https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/tree/main/examples/nextjs-dashboard> - working foundation
6. <https://api.coronium.io/api-docs/> - authoritative interactive API reference (OpenAPI 3.3.5 / Swagger UI, public)
7. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/CHANGELOG.md> - dated API and kit changes, breaking vs additive

## API endpoints you'll use

- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies` - list owned proxies
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account` - account credit, BTC and USDT balances
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies/health` - per-proxy liveness
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/tariffs/available` - in-stock tariffs with `features.p0f.count` and `features.openvpn.count` (public, no auth - use it to smoke-test connectivity)
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/free-modems?country_id=*` - stock per country, carrier and region, each row with `p0f_count` (public)
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance` - buy proxies. Body: `{tariff_id, modemCount, metadata}`. It is `modemCount`, NOT `modem_count`. Country/carrier come from the tariff; `region_id` pins a region. Optional `require: ["p0f"]`: no p0f unit = `409 p0f_unavailable`, other values = `400 unknown_requirement`, nothing charged.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-with-account-credit` - buy with USD credit
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renewal-quote` - read-only exact renewal quote
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-with-account-credit` - explicit renewal with USD credit
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/renew-modems-with-crypto-balance` - explicit renewal with BTC balance
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/restart` - rotate IP. Classic proxy: SYNCHRONOUS, `200` with `{result, rotated, ip, message}` - `rotated:false` is a failure returned as 200. There is no `?sync=true`, no `new_ip`, no 503. A row with `proxyEndpoints` answers `202` with `pending: true`: poll `GET /modems/{id}/rotation-status` until `done` or `failed`.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/rotate-modem-by-token/{token}` - token-auth rotation. `200` only on a verified new IP (`ext_ip`/`new_ip`), `502` otherwise (branch on the HTTP status, not on a body error code), `429` during the ~60 s per-modem cooldown.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-rotation-interval` - `{rotation_interval: <SECONDS>}`, minimum 60, 0 disables. Minutes are rejected with 400.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/replace` - swap broken proxy; remaining time and `metadata` are kept. A p0f line gets a p0f line or `409 p0f_replacement_unavailable` (nothing changed); body `{"allow_without_p0f": true}` accepts one without p0f. Key on `newModem._id`: `IMEI`/`portId` are deprecated aliases of it until 2026-11-19.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/p0f-options` / `PUT .../set-os` `{"os": "<value>"}` - OS fingerprint. Lines carry `features.p0f.{server_supported, supported_values, vocabulary, unavailable_reason}`; there is no `features.p0f.provider`. Refusals: `400 p0f_unsupported_on_server`, `400 p0f_os_unsupported_on_this_server`, `429` (one change per 5 min), `502 p0f_not_applied`.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/openvpn` - `.ovpn` profile. `503 openvpn_profile_pending` + `Retry-After` on a line set up in the last 2 h: retry the same line, never replace. `409 openvpn_not_supported` / `400 openvpn_disabled` are final; check the line's `features.openvpn.available`.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-metadata` - re-stamp customer mapping
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook` - register webhook URL
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook/test` - fire a real signed test event, returns the delivery result

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header. Dashboard API key lifetime 365 days. `/get-token` and `/signup` never reveal whether an account exists (`401 Invalid email or password.` for both unknown address and wrong password).

Errors on `/api/v3` return `{error, code, reason_code?, suggested_action, retryable, request_id}` plus an `X-Request-Id` header. `error` is the human string, `code` the machine id. There is no `message` field.

## Critical patterns

- **Customer mapping**: use the freeform `metadata` JSON field on each modem to track which of the reseller's end-customers owns which proxy. Send it as a JSON **string**. Every replacement keeps it. Keep a minimal local `customer_id → modem_id` record too, as recovery when the old modem is gone before your worker runs.
- **Server-side JWT**: never put `CORONIUM_API_KEY` in client-side code. All API calls go through the reseller's own server.
- **Webhook replacements**: `modem.replaced` is sent for every replacement (automatic when a modem dies, your own `POST /modems/:id/replace`, or support) and the new proxy keeps your `metadata`. Fields are nested under `data` (`data.old_modem_id`, `data.new_modem`), the envelope carries `event_id`/`occurred_at`/`account`. Deliveries are HMAC-signed (`X-Coronium-Signature`) and retried up to 8 times.
- **Idempotency**: `Idempotency-Key` header on `/payment/*` POSTs, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}`, 24h replay window. One key per buy intent, reused across retries.
- **Stock header (optional)**: Units with one login on both ports are offered without any header. `X-Coronium-Proxy-Credentials: separate-protocol-v1` on stock and purchase calls also offers units with separate HTTP/SOCKS5 logins; then read `proxyEndpoints.http` and `.socks5` and never reuse HTTP credentials for SOCKS5.
- **Capabilities, not provider**: `proxyEndpoints.provider` is an opaque label - never branch on it or show it. The one documented value is `coronium_node` (Coronium Node rows). Use `proxyEndpoints.capabilities` to decide which actions exist for a proxy.
- **Coupons**: `coupon: {coupon_name}` works on account-credit and BTC lanes, on quote, purchase and renewal. Read the applied discount from `billing.discount`; list price is `billing.subtotal_usd`.

## Don't

- Don't reinvent auto-swap or health-check logic - the backend does it.
- Don't put JWT in browser.
- Don't treat a 200 from `/restart` as a successful rotation - check `rotated`.
- Don't read webhook fields off the top level - they are under `data`.
- Don't document or depend on `proxy.expiring_soon`; the API advertises it but it never fires.
- Don't retry-loop on `409 no_stock` (`reason_code: OUT_OF_STOCK`). Ask the buyer to choose another available product.
